Subject: Re: Draft order form + MSA (Stellar / Redwood) - redlines attached

Hi Lauren / Karthik,

Thanks for the draft. Our legal team returned redlines on the MSA and the attached order form — see attached "Stellar-Redwood_OrderForm_v3.docx" and a marked PDF (MSA_Redlines_LegalTrack.pdf). The main open items are:

- Training/Data Use: we are asking for an explicit carveout so that Stellar retains ownership and exclusive control over any outputs derived from our proprietary datasets and PII, and that such data will not be used to retrain Redwood models without our written opt-in.
- Output ownership: Section 4.2 currently assigns broad rights; we want language that makes clear customer retains title to Outputs and that Redwood will have a limited operational license only for service provision and debugging.
- Feedback license / telemetry: we are willing to permit aggregated telemetry for service improvement, but want a time-limited, non-transferable license and an ability to opt out of feedback that contains sensitive user data.

Can Redwood propose counter-language for each bullet (preferably with exact redline text so we can move quickly)? Also please confirm the procurement path: do you need a PO or DocuSign first, and who on your side will own that? Our procurement lead is cc'd at legal@stellar.ai if you want to route paperwork.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we are aiming to close the order form this month.

Thanks,
Amanda Brown

Amanda — thanks for the clear notes and the tracked document. I reviewed the redlines and summarized our position below so legal can jump in with concrete language.

Quick summary of Redwood's commercial position:
- We are happy to carve out customer proprietary datasets from any automatic retraining flows.
- We are uncomfortable with absolute assignment of all "Outputs" to the customer without defining scope (e.g., outputs that are purely transformative of public models vs outputs based on Customer Content).
- For feedback/telemetry, we can accept a time-limited, non-transferable improvement license (suggest 24 months) and strict prohibitions on resale or redistribution of models that incorporate Customer Content.

Neha (cc) — can you draft redline text that: (1) clarifies that Customer retains title to Customer Content and Outputs derived solely from Customer Content; (2) gives Redwood a limited operations/debugging license; and (3) defines the permitted feedback license term and restrictions? If you provide exact text we will drop it into the MSA redline.

Karthik — want to confirm commercial flexibility on term/price adjustments if Stellar asks for a stronger opt-out (e.g., per-dataset access controls or longer retention limits).

Amanda — on procurement we typically need a signed order form (DocuSign) plus a PO for enterprise customers. If your procurement team prefers to route by PO first we can accept that; please share the PO contact.

Next steps: Neha to provide redline language today or tomorrow; we will then push back into the Word doc and reconvene for one final legal sync.

Best,

Thanks for the tags — drafting proposed redline wording below. I focused on being precise to keep negotiation cycles short. Quoted original at bottom for context.

Proposed redline snippets (to be inserted in MSA):

1) Customer Content and Output Ownership (new clause / replaces broad assignment):
"Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Content and to Outputs that are derived solely from Customer Content ("Customer Outputs"). For clarity, "Customer Outputs" does not include improvements to Redwood's models or services that are generated by combining Customer Content with non-Customer data. Redwood is granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use Customer Outputs solely to provide, maintain, and debug the Services for the benefit of Customer and to comply with its obligations under this Agreement."

2) Training and Retraining; Data Use (amend Section X):
"Redwood shall not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train, fine-tune, or retrain Redwood's foundation models or to develop derivative models for any customer or third party without Customer's prior written consent. Aggregated and de-identified telemetry that cannot reasonably be reverse-engineered to reconstruct Customer Content may be used for service improvement, provided that such telemetry excludes any Personal Data or Confidential Information."

3) Feedback License (time-limited, non-transferable):
"Customer hereby grants Redwood a limited, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Feedback provided by Customer for the purpose of improving the Services for a period of twenty-four (24) months following receipt, after which such Feedback and any derivatives thereof shall not be used for training new models. Feedback shall not include Customer Content or Customer Outputs unless Customer provides express written consent."

Operational notes / evidence request:
- We should ask Stellar for a short evidence package (catalog of dataset owners, any third-party rights statements, and confirmation of which datasets are considered proprietary) before finalizing the opt-out carveouts.
- Attach SOC2-summary.pdf for their procurement and to reduce back-and-forth on telemetry controls.

If this looks good to the commercial team I'll paste into the track-changes PDF and ask for Amanda to confirm. Happy to tighten language further if Stellar pushes back on any term.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
